questions.stem: A substance has a melting point of 1610°C, does not conduct electricity as a solid, and is very hard. What type of structure does it most likely have?

options.text: Simple molecular
Giant ionic
Giant covalent
Metallic

questions.explanation: Very high melting point, hardness, and no electrical conductivity are characteristic of a giant covalent structure (like silicon dioxide or diamond). Giant ionic structures have high melting points but their ions conduct when molten. Metals conduct as solids. Simple molecular substances have low melting points.

questions.stem: Substance Y has a high melting point, conducts electricity when molten but not when solid, and dissolves in water. What type of bonding does it have?

options.text: Covalent bonding in simple molecules
Ionic bonding in a giant lattice
Metallic bonding
Covalent bonding in a giant structure

questions.explanation: These properties are classic for ionic compounds: high melting point (strong electrostatic forces in the lattice), conducts when molten but not solid (ions are free to move when molten but fixed in the solid), and dissolves in water. Metals conduct as solids. Giant covalent structures don't usually dissolve in water. Simple molecular substances have low melting points.

questions.stem: Which substance would you expect to have the lowest boiling point?

options.text: Sodium chloride (NaCl)
Magnesium oxide (MgO)
Methane (CH₄)
Silicon dioxide (SiO₂)

questions.explanation: Methane (CH₄) is a simple covalent molecule with only weak intermolecular forces between molecules, giving it a very low boiling point (-161°C). NaCl and MgO are giant ionic structures with high boiling points. SiO₂ is a giant covalent structure with a very high boiling point. Only weak intermolecular forces need to be overcome to boil methane.

questions.stem: A student tests four substances and records the results. Which substance is most likely a metal?

options.text: Substance A: low melting point, does not conduct electricity
Substance B: high melting point, conducts electricity only when dissolved
Substance C: high melting point, conducts electricity as solid and liquid, malleable
Substance D: very high melting point, does not conduct electricity, very hard

questions.explanation: Substance C shows all the characteristics of a metal: high melting point (strong metallic bonds), conducts electricity in both solid and liquid states (delocalised electrons), and is malleable (layers can slide). A is simple molecular, B is ionic, and D is giant covalent.

questions.stem: Why can graphite conduct electricity but diamond cannot, even though both are made entirely of carbon?

options.text: Graphite is a metal and diamond is a non-metal
Graphite contains ions but diamond does not
In graphite, each carbon bonds to 3 others, leaving delocalised electrons; in diamond, each carbon bonds to 4 others with no free electrons
Diamond is harder, which prevents electron movement

questions.explanation: In graphite, each carbon atom forms only 3 covalent bonds, leaving one electron per atom delocalised and free to move. In diamond, all 4 outer electrons form covalent bonds, so there are no free electrons to carry charge. Both are giant covalent structures of carbon, but their different bonding arrangements give them different electrical properties.
